ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Sick Visit — Lorraine Hansberry — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for diarrhea during chemotherapy

text.paragraph: Watery diarrhea since yesterday, three days after chemotherapy. [S]

Ms. Hansberry called the oncology line on day 4 of her fifth cycle of modified FOLFIRINOX and was seen the same day. The pump was disconnected two days ago and pegfilgrastim given. Since yesterday afternoon she has had six watery stools, two of them overnight, and mild cramping. She took loperamide 4 mg at the first loose stool and 2 mg after each one since, eight tablets in all. Her stools are not pale or greasy as they were before pancrelipase, and there is no blood or black stool. She has had no fever (highest 37.2 °C at home), vomiting, or antibiotics, and no one around her is ill. She feels light-headed when she stands and has been drinking less than usual because of the cramps. She is eating little. Her blood glucose readings at home have been 110 to 150 mg/dL. She was writing every morning last week and wants to be back at her desk by the weekend. She has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1963-07-16; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Tired but alert; weight 53.6 kg, down 1.2 kg from the weight at cycle 4; temperature 37.1 °C
Lying 104/66 with pulse 96; standing 96/60 with pulse 112 and light-headedness: orthostatic
Head, eyes, ears, nose, and throat
Soft, mildly tender in the lower abdomen without guarding; active bowel sounds; no distension

Epigastric pain for about two months, boring through to the back and worse after meals and lying flat, with nausea, early fullness, a loss of 5 kg (8 percent of her weight), and pale, loose stools: an upper abdominal cause such as a bleeding ulcer or a pancreatic or duodenal tumor must be found. Upper endoscopy and pancreas-protocol CT booked this week
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to the documented collapse in pain and the account of a suspected duodenal ulcer. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic upper gastrointestinal blood loss: black stools on and off for three weeks, two near-fainting spells, hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL, MCV 74 fL, ferritin 6 ng/mL
S — Synthetic finding anchored to the documented account that she was told she had anemia and bleeding ulcers.

New hyperglycemia: A1c 6.6% and random glucose 132 mg/dL in a lean woman of 32 who is losing weight; new diabetes with weight loss can be the first sign of a pancreatic cancer, so it is to be confirmed and explained, not labeled type 2
S — Synthetic finding; superseded when diabetes due to the pancreatic cancer was recorded at the second visit.

Adenocarcinoma of the head of the pancreas, 3.1 cm, invading the duodenum, borderline resectable (tumor contact of more than half the circumference of the superior mesenteric vein, no arterial contact), no distant spread, CA 19-9 486 U/mL after biliary drainage; on EUS-guided biopsy; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented cancer, whose primary site the sources record differently
S — Synthetic histology, site, stage and course; the sources say she died of cancer and differ on whether it was pancreatic, duodenal, or colonic with spread to the pancreas (R). See sources.md.
Diabetes due to the pancreatic cancer (pancreatogenic, type 3c): A1c 6.6% at intake and fasting glucose 141 mg/dL
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic tumor.
Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency from obstruction of the pancreatic duct: pale, floating, loose stools after fatty meals and weight loss
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic tumor; diagnosed clinically, as guidance allows in pancreatic cancer.
Cancer-related pain in the upper abdomen and back, 6 out of 10, with sleep broken by it
S — Synthetic symptom of the synthetic tumor.
Obstruction of the distal common bile duct by the tumor, relieved by a covered metal stent placed at ERCP
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic tumor.

Chemotherapy-induced diarrhea from irinotecan, grade 2 (five to six watery stools a day above her usual), starting on day 3 of cycle 5, with low potassium and magnesium and mild dehydration; no fever, blood or neutropenia; resolved
S — Synthetic treatment effect; not a historical claim.

Oxaliplatin peripheral neuropathy, grade 1: tingling in the fingers and toes in the cold, lasting a few days after each cycle, with mild tingling at the fingertips between cycles; no effect on writing or buttons
S — Synthetic common effect of oxaliplatin.

list.item:
Chemotherapy-induced diarrhea, grade 2, from irinotecan (K52.1). Late irinotecan diarrhea, grade 2, with mild dehydration (orthostatic, creatinine 0.94 from 0.72) and losses of potassium (3.2) and magnesium (1.6). No fever, the neutrophil count is 4.1, and she has had no antibiotics, so this is uncomplicated; a stool test for Clostridioides difficile toxin was sent as a precaution and was negative later today. Not steatorrhea: the stools are watery, not pale or greasy, and she is taking pancrelipase with every meal. [S]
One liter of normal saline in the infusion center today, with magnesium sulfate 2 g intravenously.
Potassium chloride 40 mEq by mouth today, then 20 mEq daily for three days.
Loperamide 4 mg now, then 2 mg every two hours (4 mg every four hours at night) until 12 hours pass without a loose stool; oral rehydration solution.
Call at once for fever of 38.0 °C or more, blood in the stool, fainting, or diarrhea lasting beyond 24 hours on this regimen; that would need admission and octreotide.
Irinotecan reduced by one dose level (to 120 mg/m2) for cycle 6, as Dr. Adeyemi-Rourke's team agreed.

Diabetes due to the pancreatic cancer (E08.9). Glucose 118 mg/dL; eating little, so no change. [S]
Continue home glucose checks.

Pancreatic head adenocarcinoma, borderline resectable, on modified FOLFIRINOX (C25.0). Cycle 5 of six given on schedule; CA 19-9 falling at cycle 4. [S]
Cycle 6 in 11 days if the diarrhea has settled and the potassium is normal.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma (2026); Benson AB 3rd, et al. Recommended guidelines for the treatment of cancer treatment-induced diarrhea. J Clin Oncol 2004;22(14):2918-2926 (PMID 15254061) (2004)

Follow-up: Phone call tomorrow morning and blood test (potassium, magnesium, creatinine) in two days. Cycle 6 as booked if recovered. Next scheduled visit 1963-08-10: after six cycles: restaging CT and CA 19-9, decision for surgery, and preparation for pancreaticoduodenectomy. [S]
